visual_brief.subject: Claude Sonnet 5.5 coding-agent efficiency
verified_context: Anthropic kept Sonnet 5.5 list token pricing unchanged while reporting lower cost per completed task through fewer tokens, tool calls, and execution steps.
For coding-agent workloads, total task economics depend on successful completion, tool use, retries, latency, and human intervention rather than token price alone.
The practical comparison is therefore the amount of work required to reach the same accepted coding result.
visual_brief.editorial_idea: The useful economic shift is not cheaper tokens but less total machinery and work required to reach the same accepted coding result.
visual_brief.visual_metaphor: A faded, sprawling mechanical process recedes into the paper while a compact foreground mechanism reaches the same clean finished stack through a much shorter path.

candidate_notes.A: Constitution-compliant and direct, but the upper gear sequence carried too much visual weight and competed with the efficient foreground path.
candidate_notes.B: Constitution-compliant and readable, but the enclosing machine body made the metaphor feel slightly too literal and less editorial.
candidate_notes.C: Selected. The long faded process remains secondary while a compact two-gear foreground mechanism becomes the clear focal object; the same abstract inputs and finished stack make the cost-per-task idea legible without text, labels, logos, UI, or fake metrics.
